system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: At 13:40 UTC, WS-MLOPEZ-01 established a proxy tunnel to download.windowsupdate.com. The recorded user agent is Windows Update Agent, and the tunnel carried about 38.8 MB server-to-client over approximately 21 seconds.

The Windows Update traffic is consistent with a possible patch/update explanation, but the records do not identify what process initiated it or establish that it caused the reported PowerShell window.
At 14:15, WS-MLOPEZ-01 connected to DC-HD-01 over SMB and the DC recorded an ANONYMOUS LOGON network logon. The supplied records show the session, but not which share or files, if any, were accessed.
At 14:17, WS-MLOPEZ-01 connected to FILE-HD-01 over SMB, and FILE-HD-01 recorded an ANONYMOUS LOGON network logon. The records do not establish the purpose or file-level activity of this session.
The supplied records include process creation for WmiPrvSE.exe and MpCmdRun.exe, but no PowerShell process creation or command line that would confirm or explain the reported window.

known_telemetry_limitations: The provided records do not include a PowerShell process-creation event, PowerShell script-block or module logging, or a process tree for the reported time.
The proxy record identifies Windows Update traffic but does not identify the initiating process or show the content of the encrypted tunnel.
The SMB records show network sessions and logons, but do not include share-access or file-operation details.
claims_not_established: Whether PowerShell actually ran on WS-MLOPEZ-01 around 13:40 UTC, and, if so, its parent process, command line, script content, or user context.
Whether the Windows Update download was part of authorized workstation patching or was initiated by another process.
Whether the anonymous SMB sessions accessed any shares or files, or were related to the reported PowerShell window.
Whether any activity in the reviewed interval was malicious or authorized.
additional_evidence_needed: Endpoint EDR or process-audit data for WS-MLOPEZ-01 covering 13:20–14:20 UTC, including PowerShell process starts, parent-child relationships, command lines, and file activity.
PowerShell Operational logs, including script-block and module logging, plus relevant Windows process and task-scheduler logs.
Patch-management and Windows Update client logs showing whether WS-MLOPEZ-01 was being patched and which process initiated the download.
SMB server share-access and file-operation auditing on DC-HD-01 and FILE-HD-01 for the 14:15–14:17 sessions.
Relevant user, administrator, and service-account authentication or change records to establish whether the observed activity was authorized.
